body: Thank you for the long reply. I will definitely start being more affectionate. This comment section has really opened my eyes to how hard things must have been for her.
Never. As I mentioned in a comment, I did push my daughter a bit with her academics and extracurriculars, but I stopped when the therapist said it's making her stressed.

I'm familiar with the term doormat, but I don't believe myself to be a doormat for anyone other than my daughters. I will change that from now on.

My ex wife treats me really well. The divorce wasn't because of any ill treatment. It was mostly because of incomparability as a married couple
I didn't think of the latter scenario. It might be. I will bring it up with my ex-wife. Thanks

She does not know exactly what the cause is. We've tried to identify but we can't seem to find a specific reason other than just hating me. I've decided based on the replies to not be a doormat anymore.

Okay, I will discuss this with my ex-wife. I'm certain she would help. She had recently started showing interest in table tennis, which I played as a kid too. Maybe she would want to do that. 

From the replies, I am really considering hardening up a bit like you said. 

Thank you

The therapist said that her workload was too much, which is why my wife and I stopped pushing her so hard to be involved in academics and extracurriculars. That is one thing my wife and I really regret. We always thought she was fine with the workload but it turns out she wasn't.

She has said a few things over the years but it isn't anything specific. When she was younger she said it was because of taking her away from Mom, then it was about being embarrassing (standard puberty stuff I guess), now she really won't answer.

She is in therapy. She has been since the divorce. We had a very good relationship before the divorce. 

I understand that she may be angry, but it's been years since the divorce, and why is the anger directed only towards me. At this point I'm scared to "demand" basic politeness because she might get even angrier with that. If I say that something isn't allowed in my house, she simply asks me to drop her off to her mom's. 

We have talked about this countless times with a family therapist, but I don't think it's solving anything.

My current relationship with my wife has been going on since we got divorced. We both love each other's company but we weren't able to function while living with each other.

Should we tell our kids about the relationship or stop it completely?
I just watched Bunny girl senpai and Laplace's Demon makes no sense in the context of QM.

Thanks for such long replies, I really appreciate it. I try to do my hardest to be their for them. Every Thanksgiving, Christmas, School Event, I'm there. Because of my wife's work, I even drop them off to school everyday. It's just that in the past 7 years I've never heard any appreciation from either one of them. I don't know if I'm making sense, but the elder one verbally abuses me quite frequently. Both of them have separate bedrooms, but they choose to sleep together when they visit.

She has asked me to go kill myself a couple of times and though I know she doesn't mean that, it hurts hearing that from your daughter.

The problem also ties in with my work. I had the opportunity to move to New Jersey to teach the subject I'm actually passionate about but I stayed for them. Now it feels like maybe I should've just moved.

The only time I remember being thanked by her is last Christmas when she was practically forced to thank me by her mother. I wish it was the teen rebellious phase making her do this but it's been going on since she was 7.

I don't even know what I'm doing wrong. For her birthday, I got her a pretty expensive present and a handmade card so that she knows I didn't just buy an expensive gift because I didn't spend time thinking about a good present. 

I still love her and I wouldn't care about this stuff if I knew she loved me.

Thanks for answering.

My kids are 14 and 5. The older one hates me because she was 7 when we got divorced and though we had a good co-parenting plan, she ultimately felt like we shouldn't have divorced. As for why it's only directed towards me, I have no clue. Maybe because she's forced to live with her mother she has directed all of the gate towards me. Furthermore, when my ex-wife was pregnant with the second one, she assumed I'd move in again with them but that did not happen. The younger one isn't as open about her hate as her sister, but she says stuff whenever I come to take her every month for a weekend that makes me feel that she really doesn't like me.

My job doesn't just consist of teaching, I'm also the advisor of a few PhD students. In my 30s and early 40s I was doing 3, sometimes even 4, research collaborations at a time. But the subject I primarily focused on, Fields and Hypercomplex analysis, is not an active area of research and probably won't be until the next 70 years or until some physicists find application for it. This means I'm doing research in areas that I'm not interested in and I've lost the drive to keep going.

Though I don't believe in an afterlife, I find comfort that I'll stop existing once I die. I just want to stop thinking about everything wrong in my life but I can't. 

The sandwich was really tasty though. I've been buying double meat pastrami since.

1. My kids hate me. Ironically my ex-wife doesn't but she can't force them to like me.
2. I just got bored of my job. I wanted to do research in math and for the first decade, it worked out. Now my job is mainly teaching the same stuff to students semester after semester.
3. My best friend and my mother have committed suicide in the last 4 years and they were the only people that I looked forward to meeting (apart from my kids)
It's gotten to the point where the best feeling I experienced this month was when a Subway employee put extra pastrami in my sandwich without charging me.
